query: Which material can be used for lightweight and superior comprehensive performance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 high-entropy alloy exhibits superior comprehensive performance due to precipitation strengthening, where the hard L21 phase bears a larger load compared to the soft BCC matrix.
generation.intervention: High-throughput computational screening and arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements

falsification_experiment.design: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to discover lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys?. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 as successful cases). Processing: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, followed by drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific characterizations. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 700 °C) at a strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron scattering from room temperature to 1050 °C; synchrotron XRD and TEM characterization. Findings: Eight alloys were identified from 3246 initial compositions meeting criteria for Tm > 1250 °C and specific L21 phase fractions.; Alloy 1 (Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5) exhibited a yield strength of 1072 ± 25 MPa at 600 °C.; Alloy 8 (Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5) exhibited a yield strength of 1032 ± 10 MPa at 600 °C.; Both Alloys 1 and 8 maintained yield strengths of 607 ± 22 MPa and 643 ± 16
